checks.name: Frame boundaries
checks.output: 26 tests pass. A payload of exactly MAX_FRAME_BYTES (8388608) encodes to 4+8388608 bytes and decodes back to the identical payload; MAX_FRAME_BYTES+1 is refused on encode with category frame_too_large; a zero payload is refused on encode and a 0x00000000 prefix is refused on decode, both as CodecError::EmptyFrame. A stream of three concatenated frames (5-byte ASCII, a 4-byte payload containing 0x00/0xff/0x0a/0x0d, and a 4-byte-UTF-8 payload) decodes to the same three payloads under one-byte-at-a-time feeding and under every fixed chunk width from 1 up to the full stream length.

checks.name: Partial input
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test codec partial_input
checks.output: Every truncation of a 7-byte-payload frame is exercised: for 0..4 available prefix bytes the decoder returns NeedMore{additional = 4 - available}, and for 4..11 available bytes it returns NeedMore{additional = 11 - available}. Both are NonZeroUsize, so a need-more state can never claim zero outstanding bytes. A stream holding one complete frame followed by 3 bytes of a second frame yields exactly the one complete payload and leaves all 3 bytes unconsumed.

checks.name: Allocation safety
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test codec allocation_safety
checks.output: A 4-byte input of 0xffffffff (declaring 4294967295 payload bytes with no body at all) is refused as FrameTooLarge{max_bytes: 8388608, declared_bytes: 4294967295} rather than sizing anything from the prefix; a prefix of MAX_FRAME_BYTES+1 followed by 21 real bytes is refused identically, so the refusal does not depend on how much input is present. The no-allocation property itself is established from the signature and body rather than from a heap counter: decode_frame returns FrameDecode::Frame{payload: &'a [u8]} borrowed from the input and its body contains no Vec, reserve or with_capacity; the only reserve in the module is in encode_frame, sized from the caller's already-bounds-checked payload length.

checks.name: Envelope negotiation
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test codec envelope_negotiation
checks.output: A protocol name this peer does not implement yields CodecError::UnknownProtocol (wire code 1005) and an out-of-range major yields UnsupportedVersion{supported_min: 1, supported_max: 3, offered: 9} (wire code 1006); the two wire codes are asserted distinct. Versions 1, 2 and 3 are admitted. Negotiating 1..=4 against 3..=7 yields 4 in both operand orders, identical ranges yield their single version, and 1..=2 against 5..=6 yields NoVersionOverlap naming all four bounds. VersionRange::new(5, 2) fails at construction with InvertedVersionRange{min: 5, max: 2}. MajorVersion::new(0) fails with field_invalid. Four invalid protocol spellings (uppercase, doubled dot, trailing dot, leading digit) fail with field_grammar and a 65-byte name fails with field_invalid while 64 bytes passes. An *empty* range has no failing construction to observe: MajorVersion wraps NonZeroU32 and the range is inclusive, so an empty range is unrepresentable rather than rejected.

checks.name: Enum discipline
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test codec enum_discipline
checks.output: decode_security_enum accepts "allow" and refuses "allow_always" with UnknownEnumValue{field: "decision"} (wire code 1009) rather than defaulting. decode_read_only_enum returns Known for "running" and Unknown("hibernated") for an undefined spelling, with unknown_spelling() = Some("hibernated") and known() = None, so the spelling is retained without acquiring meaning. A retained spelling is still bounded: 64 bytes is accepted, 65 bytes is refused with field_invalid. Which discipline applies is fixed by which trait the type implements (SecuritySensitiveEnum vs ReadOnlyEnum), not by the caller.

checks.name: Nesting and limits
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test codec nesting_and_limits
checks.output: DepthGuard admits exactly MAX_NESTING_DEPTH = 32 levels and the 33rd enter() returns NestingTooDeep{max_depth: 32}; the depth stays at 32 after the refusal, so a refusal does not descend. A guard with ceiling 2 refuses the third level, recovers capacity after exit(), and three further exits leave depth 0 without underflow. The three ceilings fail independently and with different categories in one assertion: depth ceiling -> nesting_too_deep (code 1002), frame length ceiling -> frame_too_large (1001), field byte ceiling -> field_invalid (1003). Each ceiling is a public constant (MAX_NESTING_DEPTH, MAX_FRAME_BYTES, MAX_PROTOCOL_NAME_BYTES/MAX_REQUEST_ID_BYTES/MAX_MESSAGE_KIND_BYTES/MAX_ENUM_VALUE_BYTES).

checks.name: Error mapping
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test codec error_mapping
checks.output: All 18 CodecError variants are enumerated and matched exhaustively (a new variant is a compile error, not an untested code). The 18 wire codes 1000..=1017 are distinct after dedup and the 18 categories are distinct after dedup, so the category-to-code mapping is one-to-one and total. A hostile frame whose prefix declares MAX_FRAME_BYTES+1 followed by the literal "s3cr3t-token-do-not-log" renders a refusal that does not contain those bytes; ProtocolName::new("NOT-A-VALID-NAME") renders without echoing the rejected value; and all 18 variants render non-empty text free of the synthetic secret.

extra_checks.output: The codec test binary issues zero network syscalls (empty trace file).
